title: WebMCP Adoption Report — September 11, 2026
dek: A daily first-pass census checks the Tranco top 10,000 public domains for source-level WebMCP signals, then separates those detections from directly inspected implementation records.
changeSummary: The implementation ledger changed; review the dated finding records and evidence trails for details.

analysis.heading: Top-10,000 coverage sets the denominator
analysis.body: The first-pass Tranco census scheduled 10,000 domains and recorded 10,000 collection outcomes. It found 11 positive WebMCP source signals; 4,588 domains had no detected signal, while 782 were blocked by robots policy and 4,592 were unreachable or timed out.

analysis.heading: Deployment count overstates independent adoption
analysis.body: The best public census located for this report found 81 WebMCP-bearing provider sites, but attributed 72 of them to one ReadMe-hosted search_docs bundle. The more decision-useful number is therefore nine provider-engineered deployments, not 81 independent implementation decisions.

analysis.heading: Discovery and documentation dominate the named tool set
analysis.body: The directly inspectable external surfaces concentrate on search, markdown retrieval, llms.txt retrieval, and catalog discovery. This is a low-risk entry point: read-only tools make documentation easier for an agent to navigate without authorizing consequential business actions.

analysis.heading: Draft churn is already visible in production
analysis.body: The external census reported six deployments on the older navigator surface. Render's inspected homepage still selected navigator.modelContext on this report date. A registration can therefore exist in source while remaining unavailable to a client that implements only the current document.modelContext surface.

analysis.heading: Runtime success remains a separate claim
analysis.body: Source inspection can confirm a registration path, tool names, and schemas. It does not prove that an enabled browser exposed the tools, that an agent selected them, or that invocation completed. This report does not upgrade source evidence into runtime verification.

findings.implementation: Edge-injected WebMCP bridge plus page-owned tool manifests
findings.deploymentCountBasis: Third-party census; not independently recounted by isWebMCP.
findings.summary: Cloudflare announced a developer preview that injects a same-origin bridge at the edge and registers tool packs. Its homepage exposed a WebMCP JSON manifest with two read-only discovery tools when inspected for this report.
